rows.grounds: absolutive of √jap; indicates prior completion of recitation
compound lakṣa-traya; object denoting the number of recitations
agent noun from mantra; subject of the resulting state
past participle of √yantr; may also imply being ritually regulated or fixed
bahuvrihi compound mantra-vigraha; one whose body or form is the mantra

items.question: What transformation does chanting three hundred thousand repetitions effect in the mantra practitioner?
premises: The mantra practitioner completes three hundred thousand recitations.
This act of chanting produces a disciplined state in the practitioner.
The practitioner becomes one whose body or form is identified with the mantra.
items.inference: Through extensive mantra recitation, the practitioner attains a disciplined condition and becomes embodied as the mantra itself.
uncertainties: The precise sense of yantrito (disciplined, controlled, or ritually fixed as a yantra) is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: Having chanted three hundred thousand repetitions, the mantra practitioner becomes disciplined and takes on a mantra-body.
